title: Interradicular multilocular radiolucency of the anterior mandible
html: A 19-year-old man came to the dental school for comprehensive care. He had not seen a dentist in more than 5 years. The medical history and results of a review of systems were unremarkable, and no known drug allergies were reported. The extraoral examination revealed a well-nourished young adult with no evidence of lymphadenopathy, thyromegaly, facial swelling, or asymmetry. The intraoral examination revealed generalized caries, with mild buccal bone expansion extending to the depth of the buccal vestibule in the area of the mandibular left canine and lateral incisor.
